name: @critical-path/mcp

tools.name: list_projects
tools.description: List every project you can read, with its id, name and key. Start here to find a projectId; never guess ids. Returns { projects }.

tools.name: get_project
tools.description: Get one project by id: name, key, workflow statuses, custom field definitions and calendar. Use it before creating or moving tasks to learn the valid status keys and custom fields. Returns the project. For its tasks use `list_tasks`.

tools.name: create_project
tools.description: Create a new, empty project. Use only when the user wants a new project; to add work to an existing one use `create_task`. Returns the created project with its id.

customFields.description: Custom field values as a JSON object (validated against the project's field definitions for tasks)

tools.name: list_tasks
tools.description: Find tasks, oldest first, filtered by project, status, priority, assignee, iteration, deliverable, container or parent task ('none' for top-level tasks only). Use it for questions like "what is blocked / assigned to X / in progress" and to look up task ids. Returns { tasks, nextCursor }; pass nextCursor back as cursor for the next page. For one task's full record use `get_task`.

parentId.description: Subtasks of this task ID, or 'none' for top-level tasks only

tools.name: get_task
tools.description: Get one task by id: status, priority, assignee, estimate, logged hours, dates, blocked state and custom fields. Set includeDependencies to also see which tasks it waits for and which wait for it. Returns the task, with { dependencies: { dependsOn, dependents } } when asked. For its discussion use `list_comments`; for progress and variance use `get_task_metrics`.

includeDependencies.description: Also return the tasks this one waits for (dependsOn) and the tasks waiting for it (dependents)

tools.name: create_task
tools.description: Create a task in a project. Check with `list_tasks` first so you do not add a duplicate. Without a status the task starts in the project's default workflow status. Returns the created task with its id.

projectId.description: Project ID (inferred from active view in browser if omitted)

status.description: Status key (defaults to the project workflow's default status)

assigneeId.description: User ID to assign task to

deadline.description: Latest acceptable finish (YYYY-MM-DD for the end of that working day, or an ISO date-time). Critical path analysis reports a miss as negative slack

earliestStart.description: Earliest the task may start (YYYY-MM-DD for the start of that day, or an ISO date-time), e.g. when something from outside the project arrives

isMilestone.description: Mark the task as a milestone: a zero-duration checkpoint (release, sign-off) fed by dependencies; its estimate is ignored

allocation.description: Share of the assignee's time the task takes, in (0, 1]; e.g. 0.5 for half-time. Estimates are effort, so a 0.5 task takes twice as long

blockedReason.description: Reason why the task is blocked

customFields.description: Custom field values as a JSON object (validated against the project's field definitions for tasks)

tools.name: update_task
tools.description: Change an existing task: title, description, status, priority, assignee, due date, deadline, milestone flag, estimate, allocation, blocked state, tags or custom fields. Only the fields you pass change. Use it to move a task through its workflow or re-plan it. Returns the updated task.

status.description: Status key from the project's workflow (see `get_project`)

assigneeId.description: User ID to assign the task to

deadline.description: Latest acceptable finish (YYYY-MM-DD for the end of that working day, or an ISO date-time). Critical path analysis reports a miss as negative slack

earliestStart.description: Earliest the task may start (YYYY-MM-DD for the start of that day, or an ISO date-time), e.g. when something from outside the project arrives

isMilestone.description: Mark the task as a milestone: a zero-duration checkpoint (release, sign-off) fed by dependencies; its estimate is ignored

allocation.description: Share of the assignee's time the task takes, in (0, 1]; e.g. 0.5 for half-time. Estimates are effort, so a 0.5 task takes twice as long

blockedReason.description: Reason why the task is blocked

customFields.description: Custom field values as a JSON object (validated against the project's field definitions for tasks)

tools.name: delete_task
tools.description: Permanently delete a task by id. This cannot be undone: confirm with the user first, and prefer `update_task` with a canceled status when the history should be kept. Returns { success }.

tools.name: log_time
tools.description: Record time worked on a task. The task's logged hours are the sum of its time entries, so this is how hours are added (they cannot be set directly). Returns the time entry.

isBillable.description: Whether the time is billable (default true)

loggedAt.description: When the work was done (ISO date-time; default now)

tools.name: update_time_entry
tools.description: Correct a time entry logged with `log_time` (its id is in that result). The task's logged hours move by the difference. You can change your own entries; other people's need a project manager. Returns the entry.

loggedAt.description: When the work was done (ISO date-time)

tools.name: delete_time_entry
tools.description: Delete a time entry logged by mistake; its hours come off the task. Confirm with the user first. Returns { success }.

tools.name: add_dependency
tools.description: Record that a task cannot start until another task finishes, so the critical path schedules them in order. Use it when planning or re-sequencing work. Adding a link that already exists returns it; a link that would make a loop is refused. Returns the dependency { id, taskId, dependsOnTaskId, type }. To undo use `remove_dependency`.

dependsOnTaskId.description: The task that must finish first

type.description: 'blocking' (default) affects the schedule; 'relates_to' only links the tasks for reference

lagHours.description: Working hours to wait after the other task finishes, e.g. 16 for two working days of curing; negative to start that much earlier

tools.name: remove_dependency
tools.description: Stop a task waiting for another task, for example when the order was wrong or the work no longer depends on it. Identify the link by its two task ids, as given to `add_dependency`. Removing a link that does not exist is not an error. Returns { removed, dependencyIds } with the number of links removed.

type.description: Remove only links of this type (default: both)

tools.name: list_deliverables
tools.description: List a project's deliverables: outputs that group the tasks producing them. Use it to see what is due and which tasks feed each deliverable. For dated checkpoints, look for milestone tasks (`isMilestone`). Returns { deliverables }.

projectId.description: Project ID (falls back to ambient context if omitted)

tools.name: create_deliverable
tools.description: Create a deliverable in a project, optionally linking existing tasks by id. Use it for an output (a document, a build, an asset) that several tasks produce. For a dated checkpoint the schedule should enforce, create a task with `isMilestone: true` and a `deadline` instead. Returns the created deliverable.

projectId.description: Project ID (falls back to ambient context if omitted)

description.description: What the deliverable is and how it is accepted

taskIds.description: IDs of existing tasks that feed this deliverable

customFields.description: Custom field values as a JSON object (validated against the project's field definitions for tasks)

tools.name: list_comments
tools.description: List the comments on a task. Use it to read the discussion, decisions or blockers recorded there. Returns { comments }.

tools.name: add_comment
tools.description: Post a comment on a task, attributed to the identity this server runs as. Use it to record a decision, status note, question or the reasoning behind a change you made. Returns the created comment.

customFields.description: Custom field values as a JSON object (validated against the project's field definitions for tasks)

tools.name: calculate_critical_path
tools.description: Schedule one project with the Critical Path Method: which tasks drive the end date, each task's early and late start and finish, and how much it can slip (slack). Use it for "when will this finish?", "what is on the critical path?" or "can this task slip?". Set calendars 'assignee' with levelResources so each person works on one task at a time. Returns { projectEndDate, criticalTaskIds, tasks, overallocations }. For several projects that share people use `calculate_portfolio_critical_path`.

projectId.description: Project ID (falls back to ambient context if omitted)

calendars.description: 'assignee' schedules each task on its assignee's or team's working calendar; default uses the project calendar

levelResources.description: With calendars 'assignee': delay tasks so each assignee works on one task at a time

levelingPriority.description: Which ready task gets an assignee first when levelling (default: least slack, then task priority)

effort.description: 'remaining' schedules only estimate minus logged hours for in-progress tasks (default: full estimates)

defaultEstimateHours.description: Hours to assume for tasks with no estimate (default 1). They are listed in unestimatedTaskIds

baselineId.description: Compare with a baseline from `list_baselines`: each task reports how far it moved, and the result lists slipped tasks

tools.name: calculate_portfolio_critical_path
tools.description: Schedule several projects together (default: every project you can read) so people and teams shared between them are not double-booked. Use it for cross-project delivery dates and resource conflicts. Returns { projects, projectEndDate, overallocations } with one analysis per project. For a single project use `calculate_critical_path`.

projectIds.description: Projects to include (default: every project you can read)

projectOrder.description: Project ids in priority order for levelling; unlisted projects come last

includeHiddenWork.description: Also count other projects' work (even unreadable ones, shown only as 'hidden') toward people's capacity. Requires workspace.manage

calendars.description: 'assignee' schedules each task on its assignee's or team's calendar

levelResources.description: With calendars 'assignee': share people and team pools across the projects

levelingPriority.description: Which ready task gets an assignee first when levelling (default: least slack, then task priority)

effort.description: 'remaining' schedules only estimate minus logged hours for in-progress tasks (default: full estimates)

defaultEstimateHours.description: Hours to assume for tasks with no estimate (default 1). They are listed in unestimatedTaskIds

tools.name: create_baseline
tools.description: Save the project's current schedule as a named baseline (for example when a plan is agreed), so later analyses can show what slipped. Use the same calendars/levelResources you analyse with. Returns the baseline with its id.

projectId.description: Project ID (inferred from active view in browser if omitted)

name.description: What the plan is, e.g. "Approved plan" or "Sprint 4 start"

calendars.description: 'assignee' schedules each task on its assignee's calendar

levelResources.description: With calendars 'assignee': one task at a time per person

tools.name: list_baselines
tools.description: List a project's saved baselines, oldest first. Pass one's id as baselineId to `calculate_critical_path` to see slippage since then. Returns { baselines }.

projectId.description: Project ID (inferred from active view in browser if omitted)

tools.name: get_timeline_ladder
tools.description: Project status at three zoom levels: 'macro' phases with health (on_track, at_risk, blocked, overdue) and progress, 'standard' task timeline with the critical path and dependencies, and 'concrete' evidence of work (time logged, attachments) per task. Use it for project status reports; level 'macro' gives a compact summary. Returns { macro, standard, concrete }. For a single task use `get_task_ladder`.

projectId.description: Project ID (falls back to ambient context if omitted)

level.description: Abstraction level (macro, standard, concrete, or all)

tools.name: get_task_ladder
tools.description: One task in context: the phase it belongs to and that phase's health, its place in the schedule (dates, slack, critical or not) and evidence of work done. Use it to explain where a task fits and whether it puts its phase at risk. Returns { macroPhase, standard, concrete, metrics }. For the numbers alone use `get_task_metrics`.

tools.name: get_task_metrics
tools.description: Is a task on track? Progress percentage, actual against estimated hours, schedule variance, overdue flags and earned value (CPI, SPI). Use it to diagnose a late or over-budget task. Returns { progress, realityDelta, evm, inferredActuals, progressHistory }.

tools.name: get_task_progress_history
tools.description: How a task's progress has moved over time: dated progress points and a curve shape (linear, s_curve, early_surge, late_rush, stalled). Use it to tell whether work is stalling or being rushed at the end. Returns { points, curveProfile }. `get_task_metrics` includes the same history alongside variance and earned value.

tools.name: get_workload_distribution
tools.description: Hours of work per person, team, task type, priority or status in each day, week or month, with capacity and utilization. Use it for "who is overloaded?" and capacity planning; a utilizationRatio above 1 means more work than capacity. Omit projectId for the whole workspace. Returns { buckets, seriesKeys, seriesLabels, totalHours, averageUtilization }.

projectId.description: Project ID (optional, defaults to workspace-wide or ambient project)

defaultWeeklyCapacityHours.description: Default weekly capacity hours per person (default 40)

tools.name: get_skill
tools.description: Load a step-by-step playbook for a multi-step project management job, such as planning a project, triaging tasks, finding schedule risk, writing a status report, checking capacity or investigating a late task. Call it before starting such a job and follow its steps. Omit name to list the skills. Returns { name, description, content }, or { skills } without a name.

name.description: Skill name, e.g. "plan-project"; omit to list all skills

instructions:
Critical Path is a project management backend. A project holds tasks and deliverables (outputs that group the tasks producing them). Tasks have a workflow status, priority, assignee, effort estimate, logged hours, optional subtasks (parentId) and dependencies, and comments. A task with `isMilestone: true` is a zero-duration checkpoint, and a `deadline` on any task is enforced by critical path analysis.

Working rules:
- Never guess ids. Get them from list or create results.
- Results are JSON objects. List results are paged where they return nextCursor; pass it back as cursor.
- Status values are keys from the project's workflow; read them from get_project before setting one.
- Confirm with the user before any tool marked destructive.

Which tool to use:
- Find a project or task id: list_projects, list_tasks
- Read one task, then its discussion: get_task, list_comments
- Add or change work: create_task, update_task, create_deliverable
- Order work: task B cannot start until task A finishes: add_dependency, remove_dependency
- What a task waits for and what waits for it: get_task
- A dated checkpoint (release, sign-off): a task with isMilestone and a deadline: create_task
- Record hours worked, or correct them: log_time, update_time_entry, delete_time_entry
- Record a decision or note on a task: add_comment
- "When will it finish?" / "What is critical?": calculate_critical_path
- Dates and conflicts across several projects: calculate_portfolio_critical_path
- Save the agreed plan, or "what slipped since the plan?": create_baseline, list_baselines, calculate_critical_path
- Project status and phase health: get_timeline_ladder
- "Is this task on track?" / why is it late: get_task_metrics, get_task_ladder, get_task_progress_history
- "Who is overloaded?" / capacity: get_workload_distribution

For multi-step jobs, load the matching skill with get_skill { name } before you start, and follow it:
- analyze-schedule: Find what drives a project's end date, how much each task can slip and where people are double-booked, then recommend fixes. Use for "when will we finish?", "what is critical?" or deadline-risk questions.
- investigate-task: Work out why a specific task is late, stalled or over budget and what it puts at risk. Use when the user asks about one task's status, delay or overrun.
- plan-capacity: Check who is overloaded or idle over a time window and rebalance assignments. Use for capacity planning, workload balancing or "can we take on more work?" questions.
- plan-project: Turn a goal, brief or feature list into a Critical Path project with deliverables, estimated and prioritized tasks, and the dependencies between them. Use when the user asks to plan, scope or break down work.
- report-status: Write a project status report covering progress, phase health, forecast finish, risks and blockers, backed by the schedule and metrics. Use when the user asks how a project is going or wants a status update.
- triage-tasks: Review new, unprioritized or stale tasks and set priority, estimate, tags and blocked state consistently. Use when the user asks to triage, groom or clean up a backlog.
